## Features

| Feature | Symphony Sleep Sense |
|---|---|
| Motor control | Product-specific individual and combined actuators, including SS800's fifth actuator |
| Position feedback | None; sleep measurements are not motor positions |
| Presets | Product-specific recall; explicit save on ES700, SS800 and HILO |
| Memory | Two recalls normally, one on HILO, none on ST800 |
| Massage | Six distinct legacy page projections; sonic BED massage on selectors 8 and 9 independently of product |
| Lights | Toggle on legacy pages; explicit on/off, color codes and brightness on ES700/SS800; none on 400E/HILO |
| Bed alarm | Product-specific mode, clock/calendar and split-side handling |
| Privacy | Settings actions for selectors 2 and 9 |
| Automatic anti-snore | Head/Elevation, format-specific strength and demonstration |
| Firmware/protocol | Read-only Device Information, including exact SENSOR_VOICE privacy interpretation |

## Choosing a profile

Choose **Symphony Sleep Sense**, then the product and BLE selector shown by the
app. Shared names and services do not identify this app or its product. Unknown
product and unknown selector retain the app's explicitly labelled fallbacks.

### Aliases

The bed type is `symphony`. Existing Okin, Keeson and SleepEase entries retain
their separate app profiles. Selecting Symphony is an explicit setup change.

## Wire codec

### Transports

| Role | Service | Characteristic |
|---|---|---|
| Nordic UART write | `6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` | `6e400002-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` |
| Nordic UART notify | `6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` | `6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` |
| Alternate write | `0000ffe5-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` | `0000ffe9-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` |
| Alternate notify | `0000ffe0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` | `0000ffe4-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` |
| Firmware | `0000180a-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` | `00002a26-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` |
| App-labelled protocol | `0000180a-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` | `00002a27-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` |

When both transports exist, later matching services overwrite each role
independently. Commands use acknowledged writes. Notifications are subscribed
before startup queries. A confirmation query on selectors 8/9 does not require
a payload acknowledgement before normal app operation. No peripheral pairing or
authentication guarantee follows from that observation.

### Framing and checksum

P1 uses the existing [Keeson codec](keeson.md): E6, FE16, four little-endian word
bytes, a side byte and the complemented byte-sum checksum. P3 uses existing
[Okin N-frames](okin-nframe.md), including 40-bit keys and calendar/alarm records.
P2 uses AA writes and 2A queries: two zero bytes, domain, operation, an
operation-specific size and payload. P2 has no universal checksum or receive
length assembler. Its light operation's size is not its payload byte count.

The product controls select the builder. Model 15 position/preset helpers force
P1 and side 1/2; model 10 forces P3 and side 1/2. Their light callback remains
generic. ES700/SS800 preset and light builders are fixed P2. SS800's fifth
actuator is fixed P2. HILO Reading/TV recalls and every supported save use their
fixed P3 helpers. HILO's combined axes 3+4 use P2 for selectors 8/9 and P3
otherwise. These exceptions do not change generic driver selection.

### Responses

Short inputs under three bytes are dropped before fragment processing. Only an
original 20-byte input with FE16 at bytes 1/2 is cached and joined to the next
eligible notification. Reconnecting clears that cache.

P2 light replies must have exactly 12 bytes. Alarm, massage and anti-snore
branches require all fields they access, including disabled/off responses.
Additional trailing bytes remain accepted where the source accepts them.
HA rejects malformed packets atomically instead of copying the app's
RangeError and partially corrupted anti-snore state.

### STOP and release behavior

Motor holds send once on press. P1 base release waits 300 ms; forced P1 split
and P3 release wait 100 ms. P2 sends driver STOP then command STOP immediately.
The controller owns and awaits captured release frames, side and session, even
after cancellation. It never rereads a mutable command for delayed cleanup.
There is no proven movement refresh interval or concurrent-motor composition.

### Vectors

`tests/test_symphony_vectors.py` checks all 122 frozen literal constructions and
49 final frame/parameter cases. The controller tests exercise elapsed holds,
malformed responses, source projections, independent model/selector choices,
and session cleanup. These are simulated BLE results.

## Profiles

### Symphony Sleep Sense

**App:** [Symphony Sleep Sense](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.okin.ist) 2.8.0 (194), `com.okin.ist`

**Status:** ❓ Static behavior verified; hardware unverified.

#### Setup

Product selection is explicit. The name rule uppercases the platform name and
accepts contains SMARTBED/OKIN, or SLEEP with manufacturer data. Manufacturer
0x59 and ordered name overrides determine the selector, with OKIN last. The
manufacturer-derived six-byte logical name does not replace the BLE address.
The setup chooser offers this app alongside stronger existing receiver matches.
The standalone split-head side is configurable; paired child targets retain
their own side and each receiver's product/selector fields.

#### Controls

The product table governs actuator and entity availability. A local child-mode
selector suppresses ordinary controls; it is an HA app preference, not a
hardware lock or authentication. STOP and the source's privacy action bypass
that local control gate.

Recall and save are distinct actions. P2's short-release recall and 5.5-second
hold save are exposed explicitly. Generic 6.5-second long-press toasts do not
program memory. HILO's held Save modifier is represented by explicit save
actions, and Flat never gains an invented save action.

#### Timing

Held motion uses elapsed monotonic deadlines, independent of write ACK time.
Renewable motor leases are latched; finite presets retain finite behavior.
The user pulse count/delay bounds ordinary motor presses and supplies no
inferred firmware refresh cadence. All delayed requested writes stay inside
their admitted command lane and current connection generation.

Clock sync uses one local calendar snapshot. P1 sends that identical snapshot
twice synchronously. Selector 5 uses BCD time/calendar fields; selector 2 and
the other selectors keep their own year/month/weekday transforms. The
SoundWave alarm page uses its fixed P2 calendar builder.

#### Notifications

The massage sensor reports the app's timer **index**, not countdown telemetry.
The six legacy pages remain distinct: combined strength is only logged by the
app and is not invented as a seventh UI state. Premier runs when head strength
is positive; its display is zero or the received time index followed by a
literal zero. The wave reversal does not supply that display value.

All seven alarm bindings retain their source offsets, mode maps and BCD
differences. Disabled SoundWave alarms retain cached mode/week/time. Split P1
set and close require a sufficiently long fresh peer response; no response is
padded. Split P3 checks the opposite enabled, nonzero record for the exact same
hour/minute, without a week-overlap test. Unknown or stale peer state prevents
the requested write. No alarm list or firmware slot capacity is synthesized.

Partial color/brightness changes query fresh light state first. Explicitly
providing both parameters also works. The app's cold-cache clamps to color 1
and brightness 20 are not published as hardware defaults. Sonic massage
parameter cycles likewise hydrate their current session state.

#### Services

| Action | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `symphony_set_alarm` | Set or close the product's alarm; weekdays use Monday 1 through Sunday 7 |
| `symphony_set_light` | Explicit color code 1–7 and brightness 20–80 on ES700/SS800 |
| `symphony_anti_snore` | Head/Elevation, enabled state, source-specific strength, or demonstration |
| `symphony_preset` | Explicit recall/save for the chosen product |
| `sync_clock` | Source-specific bed clock synchronization |
| `timed_move`, `hold_control` | Bounded motors and renewable motor leases |

Family services validate every target before requested writes and capture STOP
admission before connection or hydration. The opaque bed diagnostic button
sends only the app's fixed diagnostic query; it does not claim an unverified
physical effect and is not a raw-packet API.

#### Evidence

Accepted row133 establishes three direct BLE wire groups, explicit product and
selector dispatch, parser bindings and release behavior. Static controls are
implemented without requiring maintainer hardware testing. External beta/release
reports can corroborate peripheral effects and transport behavior.

## Notes

Wi-Fi provisioning, network administration, cloud/accounts, OTA transfers,
phone/speaker/music controls and sleep-report analytics are outside this
integration. Firmware reads and BED session ownership remain supported.
No sleep/history/vitals quantity becomes a motor position.

Historical sleep transfers, assembly, scoring, SQL persistence and upload are
outside this integration. Their transfer-specific batching, callback replacement
and conditional confirmations are likewise excluded: HA neither starts nor
consumes those transactions. Unsolicited history does not replace BED callbacks
or trigger confirmations. Normal bed controls keep the shared serialized writer,
current-session notification ownership and captured delayed cleanup. Reader's
generic preset toast is a bed caller, not a history transfer.

Sequential two-address alarm operations hydrate and validate again inside each
executing session after topology switching. Split P1 Both edits are composed
into one complete peer-preserving table. Split P3 cannot give both sides the
same enabled alarm time.

Renewable holds require simultaneous side execution. Select Left or Right on a
non-native single-address pair or a sequential pair; Both leases are rejected
before motion and are not advertised by the card. Finite Both actions remain
available.
